title: SMP userspace scheduler non-PELT rollout
summary: Non-PELT SMP scheduler witnesses remain useful, and PELT stays explicitly out of scope, but fresh OSComp libcbench 1x/4x evidence does not show a default performance win. OSComp performance promotion is blocked until a non-PELT child-spread or movable-userspace gate is made explicit and measured with owner counters.

steps.title: Align active reactor, scheduler, SMP, and ThreadRuntime contracts
steps.notes: Canceled for the 2026-08-09 non-PELT closeout. The original contract-alignment pass was a broader pre-implementation gate for the PELT-era plan; this closeout records the already-landed non-PELT behavior and does not edit active design docs.

steps.notes: Canceled for this worktree closeout. The broader TaskControl/RunToken/PollLease authority refactor was not required to accept the current non-PELT performance path; the accepted path is bounded to the existing scheduler metadata plus userspace-run token unwind tests.

steps.title: Close wake, IPI coalescing, trap-return, and WFI races
steps.notes: Canceled for this worktree closeout. The wake/IPI/WFI race model remains future correctness work if reopened; it is not needed to claim the current depth/direct-steal/movable-userspace performance improvement.

steps.title: Accept S1 authoritative SMP correctness
steps.notes: Canceled as an original broad S1 authority gate. The completed non-PELT closeout is intentionally narrower: host scheduler semantics plus movable SMP guest stress, without declaring the full wake/IPI/TaskControl model production-complete.

steps.title: Enable and accept static AP userspace placement
verification: cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case static --timeout-ms 60000
steps.notes: Parse immutable legacy/static/movable and depth load modes. Static mode spreads four user tasks across four harts and pins each after placement; excluding the owner remains ENOSYS until S3. The RV64/QEMU witness lane has a stable 2x guest pass with worker-window publish coverage `[0,1,2,3]`. This non-PELT closeout does not promote or require pelt-shadow/pelt modes.

steps.title: Validate full userspace token unwind before migration
steps.notes: Every userspace round trip carries TaskKey, run_seq, and hart; syscall, fault, timer, and Reschedule paths clear old identity/payload/token slots and inactive resume context before publishing Preempted. Trap-shell handoff now rejects pending entry tokens and stale request ids through `complete_running_trap`, while timer-preempt placeholders remain replaceable by a later real trap. The hart-local userspace slot is cleared on the actual entry hart before repoll.

steps.title: Add idle-first direct steal and forced affinity migration
steps.notes: Only `Preempted.front` is stealable; the thief cannot bypass an ineligible front or scan New/Boosted queues. Forced affinity handles Parked, Queued, and Polling separately and cannot return userspace on a disallowed hart.

steps.title: Accept movable userspace with SMP guest stress
verification: cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case affinity --timeout-ms 120000
cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case pipe --timeout-ms 120000
cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case timer --timeout-ms 120000
cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case pthread --timeout-ms 120000
cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case mixed --timeout-ms 120000
cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case stress --timeout-ms 120000
steps.notes: Accepted movable userspace with the full SMP scheduler witness case driver. Initial userspace now stays on the current boot hart so the first reactor loop drives the published init task immediately instead of publishing to CPU0 from a non-CPU0 boot hart. The witness cases now pass for pipe, affinity, timer, pthread, mixed, and stress under `tx.sched.smp=movable tx.sched.load=depth tx.sched.case=<case>`; pipe/mixed/stress use any worker to claim the pipe-writer role, and pthread is a bounded futex syscall witness rather than the previously crashing extra raw-clone pthread shape. The raw-clone pthread stack/page-fault path remains a separate kernel follow-up, but it no longer blocks S3 movable scheduler acceptance.

steps.title: Run final host and guest matrix and catch up active docs
verification: cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case pipe --timeout-ms 120000
cargo xtask test smp-scheduler-witness --target rv64-qemu --case affinity --timeout-ms 120000
steps.notes: Blocked for OSComp performance promotion under the user-approved non-PELT scope. The SMP scheduler witnesses still cover depth spread, idle-first direct steal, forced affinity migration, periodic rebalance, and movable userspace mechanics, but fresh RV64 OSComp `libcbench-musl` evidence did not show a 4-core win: SMP1 default summed 5.877901s across 27 time rows with judge 31.17261685982155/27; SMP4 default summed 6.091749s with judge 30.67807807933117/27. A cfg-only `tx_userspace_child_spread_smp4` oracle reached group end and improved SMP4 to 6.039818s / judge 30.874192297415338/27, but still lost to SMP1. PELT and segmented storage remain unimplemented; next is an explicit child-spread or movable-userspace boot gate plus counters before any OSComp performance claim.

risks: Queue and task authority can remain split if compatibility methods survive outside the transition core.
A Reschedule IPI can still miss userspace arbitration if ack, ipi_armed, and polling-idle ordering are changed independently.
Movable userspace is unsafe until every trap path clears the exact old-hart run token and resume context.
Do not infer full raw-clone pthread create/join production correctness from the bounded futex pthread witness; the raw-clone page-fault path remains separate follow-up.
Do not reopen PELT or segmented storage from this plan without a new user decision and fresh matched evidence.
